# Job Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 416r–416v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_001_page_001.jpg, JOB_001_page_002.jpg

---

**1:1** A-man there-was in-the-land of-Uts [Uz], Iyyov [Job] [was] his-name; and-was the-man that blameless [tam] and-upright [yashar], and-fearing God [elohim], and-turning-away from-evil [ra].

**1:2** And-were-born to-him seven sons and-three daughters. **1:3** And-was his-livestock [miqneh]: seven-thousand sheep, and-three-thousand camels, and-five-hundred yoke of-oxen, and-five-hundred female-donkeys, and-servants [avodah] very many; and-was the-man that great [gadol] from-all the-sons of-the-east [qedem].

**1:4** And-went his-sons and-made a-feast [mishteh] [at] the-house of-each-one [on] his-day; and-they-sent and-called to-their-three sisters to-eat and-to-drink with-them. **1:5** And-it-was when-went-around the-days of-the-feast, Iyyov would-send and-sanctify-them [vayeqaddishem], and-he-rose-early in-the-morning and-offered-up burnt-offerings [olot] [according to] the-number of-all of-them; for said Iyyov, "Perhaps my-sons have-sinned [chat'u] and-blessed [vaberku] God in-their-hearts." Thus did Iyyov all the-days.

**1:6** And-it-was the-day, and-came the-sons of-God [benei ha-elohim] to-present-themselves [lehityatsev] upon YHWH, and-came also the-Adversary [ha-satan] in-their-midst. **1:7** And-said YHWH to the-Adversary, "From-where do-you-come [tavo]?" And-answered the-Adversary YHWH and-said, "From-roaming [mi-shut] in-the-earth and-from-walking-about [me-hithalekh] in-it."

**1:8** And-said YHWH to the-Adversary, "Have-you-set [ha-samta] your-heart upon my-servant [avdi] Iyyov? For there-is-none like-him in-the-earth — a-man blameless and-upright, fearing God and-turning-away from-evil."

**1:9** And-answered the-Adversary YHWH and-said, "Is-it for-nothing [chinam] that Iyyov fears God? **1:10** Have-you not made-a-hedge [sakta] around-him and-around his-house and-around all that [is] his on-every-side? The-work of-his-hands you-have-blessed [berakta], and-his-livestock [miqneh] has-spread [parats] in-the-land. **1:11** But stretch-out [shelach] now your-hand and-touch [nega] all that [is] his — surely [im lo] to your-face he-will-bless-you [yevarekekha]."

**1:12** And-said YHWH to the-Adversary, "Behold, all that [is] his [is] in-your-hand; only upon him do-not stretch-out your-hand." And-went-out the-Adversary from-the-presence of-YHWH.

**1:13** And-it-was the-day, and-his-sons and-his-daughters [were] eating and-drinking wine in-the-house of-their-brother the-firstborn. **1:14** And-a-messenger [malakh] came to Iyyov and-said, "The-oxen were plowing and-the-donkeys were-grazing beside-them, **1:15** and-the-Sabeans [Sheva] fell [upon them] and-took-them, and-the-servants [ne'arim] they-struck with-the-edge of-the-sword; and-escaped only I alone to-tell you."

**1:16** While-this-one [was] still speaking, this-one came and-said, "The-fire of-God [esh elohim] fell from-the-heavens and-burned among-the-sheep and-among-the-servants and-consumed-them; and-escaped only I alone to-tell you."

**1:17** While-this-one [was] still speaking, this-one came and-said, "The-Chaldeans [Kasdim] set three bands [rashim] and-rushed [vayifshetu] upon the-camels and-took-them, and-the-servants they-struck with-the-edge of-the-sword; and-escaped only I alone to-tell you."

**1:18** While-this-one [was] still speaking, this-one came and-said, "Your-sons and-your-daughters [were] eating and-drinking wine in-the-house of-their-brother the-firstborn, **1:19** and-behold, a-great wind [ruach gedolah] came from-across the-wilderness and-struck the-four corners of-the-house, and-it-fell upon the-young-people [ne'arim] and-they-died; and-escaped only I alone to-tell you."

**1:20** And-rose Iyyov and-tore [vayiqra] his-robe [me'il] and-shaved [vayagaz] his-head, and-fell to-the-ground [artsah] and-bowed-down [vayishtachu]. **1:21** And-he-said, "Naked [arom] I-came-out from-the-womb of-my-mother, and-naked I-shall-return there. YHWH gave [natan] and-YHWH took [laqach]; may-the-name of-YHWH be blessed [mevorakh]."

**1:22** In-all this Iyyov did-not sin [lo chata], and-did-not ascribe [natan] unseemliness [tiflah] to-God.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "land of Uz":** The location of Uz (*Uts*) is debated — possibly Edom or Aram. The name places Job outside Israel, establishing his universality from the first word.

**v.5 — "blessed God":** The Hebrew *vaberku elohim* uses the euphemism *barakh* ("bless") for "curse." The scribes substituted "bless" to avoid writing "curse God." This occurs four times in Job 1-2.

**v.6 — "the Adversary":** Hebrew *ha-satan* — with the definite article, indicating a role ("the accuser/adversary") rather than a proper name. This is not the later "Satan" of Christian theology but a member of the divine council.

**v.21 — "naked I came out":** The Hebrew *arom* echoes the creation narrative. Job's response is the theological center of chapter 1 — radical acceptance framed in liturgical language.

*— EMET*
